utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir. General Obradovic, my name is Djuro Cepic and I am one of the Defence counsel for General Vladimir Lazarevic. First of all, I would like to greet you here.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I will be asking you some questions about 1998, the period while you were in the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army. General, do you know that the Pristina Corps in 1998 had its forward command post at Djakovica in order to coordinate the activities securing the state border?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got that as part of our operative reports from our subordinate commands, indicating that the forward command post of the corps had been set up in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know who was in charge of the forward command post of the Pristina Corps in Djakovica in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that, and when the team from the General Staff visited this area I was able to see that for myself. There was the Chief of Staff of the corps, I think it was Colonel Lazarevic at the time, I think he was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, you mentioned it now, and yesterday you stated that in your evidence, that in mid-August with the team of the General Staff headed by General Perisic you visited the Pristina Corps units in the garrison in Djakovica. My question to you is: Do you perhaps remember who was there to meet this team at the Djakovica forward command post on behalf of the corps?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was in the team headed by General Perisic, Chief of General Staff, as we went there to check the 3rd Army units with our focus on the Pristina Corps units and when we went from the Pristina garrison to the Djakovica garrison we were met by Colonel Lazarevic, Chief of Staff of the corps, at the forward command post in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, did the chain of command in the Pristina Corps, was it in line with all the rules and regulations since you checked all that at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since my sector dealt with those issues, the sector that I headed, as we did this check we also checked the command system in the subordinate commands. And at the end of the analysis we concluded that the command system was not functioning fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, we have a problem with transcript. It is completely opposite, if you see page 91 and line 11 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you answer the question again, please, Mr. Obradovic, which was: Did the chain of command in the Pristina Corps, was it in line with all the rules and regulations when you made the check in mid-August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my response was yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned the analysis that you undertook. General, this team from the General Staff after doing this check, did it actually analyse this check and did it present the results at the meeting or at a briefing in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the methodology of the team from the General Staff after the activity was completed, after the garrisons and commands were toured, that an analysis be made and that the chief conclusions be presented that the situation be described. And that kind of an analysis was done at the time when the team completed its work checking the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, am I right to -- when I say that at this briefing in Pristina Colonel Lazarevic was not there because he remained at the forward command post in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole of the team from the General Staff was there at the analysis and the commander of the army and the commander of the corps. The commander of the army was Samardzic at the time and the corps commander was General Pavkovic. And Colonel Lazarevic was at the forward command post at a different garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have in e-court system Exhibit Number 5D194, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, now we will very briefly deal with 1999. Today you said in your evidence that as of March you were at the head of the 2nd Army, headquartered in Podgorica. Let us just wait for the document to appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we also have a version in English language and I hope that we will see in next couple of seconds or minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, could you please look at the last three paragraphs in this document. Do you recognise that this is a document from the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that at the heading and you can see the signature by Commander Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please now look at the last three paragraphs. Could you please read the paragraph that begins with the words: "In order to prevent ..."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In order to prevent the pulling out and spilling out of the Siptar terrorist forces from the Rugovska Klistura sector to Montenegro, it is necessary to ensure that the Podgorica Corps units block the following line Cakor pass --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, we don't want to waste any time. Do you perhaps remember any incidents from that period related to organisation or coordination of the activities of the Podgorica Corps which was part of the activities of the Pristina Corps [as interpreted] which was part of the 3rd Army in order to neutralise strong terrorist forces in the broader Rugovska Klistura area in April and later May 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. It was one of the tasks that the Podgorica Corps received, to establish coordination and cooperation with the adjacent units of the Pristina Corps in order to carry out the task listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. This was my last question. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, General Obradovic, I am Dan Ivetic, and I have just a few questions for you so hopefully I'll be brief. Now, first of all I'd like to ask you if it's correct pursuant to your understanding of the Law on Defence as to resubordination of the MUP during times of war that units of the MUP were to be engaged in combat operations in accordance with their purposes in the areas pursuant to a decision of the VJ komandant.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That order was issued by the supreme staff command because at that time, that was some ten days after the aggression against the federal republic started, the situation was such that the assessments were that quite soon the ground forces could be deployed from the broader base of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the assessment was that in order to resist the aggression the MUP units should be also used in combat, and that is why an order was issued to resubordinate MUP elements to the army commands in that area, and that would be the 2nd and the 3rd command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move to your document, it was used in direct examination, P1905, just see if I can perhaps clarify the question to get the information we're looking for. This is the letter which is identified in the witness notification as the letter written by yourself regarding subordination of the Montenegrin MUP units, but as we've heard today the -- no one seems to care about the Montenegrin MUP and we're talking about the Serbian MUP. So I'd like to ask you specifically with respect to this document. The bottom of page 1 in B/C/S or Serbian and the second paragraph on page 2 in English. Am I correct that in that section your own words state that: "MUP units will be engaged in combat operations in accordance with their purposes in the areas pursuant to the decisions of the VJ commander." And I want to ask you again: Is that your understanding of how the Law of Defence regarding resubordination of MUP units operated -- was to operate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Law of Defence envisaged or stipulated that during combat MUP units could be deployed to resist the enemy in accordance with their specific type of use. This was how the order was issued, that there should be coordination, organisation, and that MUP units should take part in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I'm trying to ask a very specific question where you say that during combat MUP units could be deployed. Am I correct they could be deployed upon an order or a decision or a directive by the VJ komandant in that region, as is stated in your letter?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't fully understand your question because I don't have it here in front of me what you just asked me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's page 1 of the Serbian, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Page 1, bottom of page 1, it should be the last paragraph in the -- beginning -- in the middle of that paragraph in the Serbian, I could -- well, let me do it this way. This might make it easier for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you see in this letter on the first page in Serbian about the involvement of the MUP units it says that: "The MUP units in combat will be used in accordance with their purpose in the zones in accordance with the decisions of the VJ commander." I just wanted you to confirm that the deployment of the MUP units is based on some kind of an order or decision of the VJ commander in that area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this decision had been carried out the way that it was drafted, that the MUP should be resubordinated, then it would have been the case. But since the decision was not definitive enough, it was not defined enough, then the MUP units were not used within the chain of command of the army but there was just coordination between the MUP units and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [In English] I apologise. I have to pause to allow the translation and the transcript to catch up with us. During the time-period following the commencement of the NATO bombings, specifically from the time-period when you were appointed as the commander of the 2nd Army through the period of the NATO aggression against Yugoslavia, the time of war, am I correct that in your region as, far as the language we have just quoted is concern, you would be the komandant of the VJ that would issue orders for ground combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the authority based on the chain of command. The commanders in the zones based on the chain of command, if the decisions were made at the army command or corps command, the chain of command functioned here so that everybody knew based on the task that was issued what they have to do and when and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, I apologise, I'm having to wait for the translation and the transcript to make sure that I don't cause complications in the understanding of what's being said here. Now, during this same time-period, that is to say from when you were appointed as commander of the 2nd Army, which was a few days after the NATO bombing began, through the end of the NATO -- the war with NATO, let's put it that way, would you kindly identify any order, instruction, or decision issued by you to engage in ground combat operations or "borbena dejstva" so that there's no misunderstanding on the territory of Serbia that you issued or directed to the MUP of Serbia that was refused or rejected to be carried out by the organs of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this suggestion in your question -- well, there's no need to explain it because I didn't have any powers in the area of responsibility to issue any commands to the MUP and for those units to carry out those orders. As for any tasks according to the chain of command, that belonged to the army troops. Since you asked me about the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, that was definitely not the case and that is not how things were done.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you for the same time-period, did you issue any decisions, directives, or orders for the commencement of any "borbena dejstva," ground combat operations on the territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, although the greater part of the area of responsibility was in the territory of the Republic of Serbia, I did not issue any orders with regard to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I apologise for any inconvenience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, if your letter to the MUP of Serbia had been answered and if MUP units were resubordinated to the VJ, would they then have had to act in accordance with orders given by commanders of VJ units in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, let me state that that was not materialised, or rather, the MUP was not resubordinated to the army, including the 2nd Army, that had parts of both territories within its area of responsibility. We discussed that already, why this was the case. This decision, had it been carried out, it would have been whatever, then we would have had a new situation. However, since this new situation did not come into being, the only thing I can do is comment on what happened in reality. Had this task been carried through, I probably would have had a different comment and I could have conveyed to you a different kind of experience in terms of what had been done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's what I want an answer to. What would have happened had resubordination taken place? Would you then have been issuing orders which the MUP had to comply with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, had that order been carried out, then it would have been in the function of an order being issued by a superior command, it would have been gone down the chain of command. However, since this task was not materialised, I'm saying that there was no need to think about that or to discuss that in any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You don't need to say that yet again. Just deal with the question I'm asking you, and you've dealt with it. But I know that it didn't happen. I don't need to be told four or five times. Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'd like to first ask about your evidence in respect to Podujevo, and I think you said that the unit that was involved in an exchange with the KLA had been sent down there for training and were involved in training, and that was your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That unit was sent to the training grounds in order to have training carried out, because in the meantime young soldiers had come in. We were talking about the replacements that had to be additionally trained because they were insufficiently trained. Their aptitude and level of training could have been tested successful only at the training grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where these training grounds were, you said that it was in the vicinity of a key road, a key line of communication?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those training grounds are in the area between Pristina and Podujevo, the so-called Malo Kosovo. That is the road between Pristina and Podujevo and further on to Merdare and Kursumlja. Batlova is the name of the training grounds, and there is an airfield there too where part of the Pristina Corps units from the Pristina garrison were trained.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And that was a key communication line, key line of communication?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was an important communication line linking the central part of Serbia with Kosovo, that is to say going from Merdare, Prokuplje, Kursumlja, Podujevo, Pristina, and further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Had there been KLA activity in that area before, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is known that there had been activity like that before that in that area too, before that time, that is, because this communication was important and the terrorists tried to keep this line of communication under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In those circumstances, wouldn't it -- or question withdrawn. The -- having regard to the tension in the area and the fact that there were terrorists, as you call them, activity in the area before, wasn't the placing of this unit in that vicinity clearly provocative in your view?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In no case could this constitute a form of provocation because according to the plan with all the measures that were taken, the OSCE was notified that the unit was going out there and what its task was and where it would be staying. There was no reason for irritation or taunting the terrorists in any way for them to engage. So it could not be a problem on account of its activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was the OSCE notified as to the purpose that this unit was going there for?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've already discussed this today. They were informed substantially about the unit itself, then the place where it would be carrying out various activities, and that was a unit that was well-known from the 15th Armoured Brigade and the content of their activities, too, and it focused on training young soldiers. Just one more comment. What you asked me about, Mr. Prosecutor, if it were that kind of purpose, no one ever would have sent a unit consisting of young soldiers there, untrained, unequipped; they would be easy prey to the terrorists, the terrorists could easily attack that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think you said in evidence that General Dimitrijevic was the chief of army security and kept close watch on what was happening in Kosovo on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, General Dimitrijevic was chief of the administration for security in the General Staff. Through his organs from his own line of work he followed and analysed the situation in Kosovo as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we bring up P928, please, this is a record of the collegium meeting of the 30th of December, 1998, and if we go to page 14 in the English version which corresponds to page 15 in the B/C/S version, and in the B/C/S version as the fourth paragraph from the top where General Dimitrijevic is speaking. It's not on that page, if I may advise the Court, it is -- he begins speaking on the previous page, page 13 of the English version, but he continues here: "In addition the current situation in the vicinity of Podujevo, I think that we must be completely consistent here and completely open towards each other, so to speak. This situation in Podujevo and the surroundings, it was complex before, but when did it suddenly become even more complicated. After the so-called pretend or real planned combat exercises in which this company took part in the field. General, these sort of moves will lead us to disaster, the explanation that this was not a planned exercise, this is not true, it was planned so that the MUP would provoke the terrorists so that the MUP would have to do whatever it would have to do."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall General Dimitrijevic expressing this view as to what was happening in Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that. This was a statement made by General Dimitrijevic; however, on the basis of all the others -- well, it's some kind of conclusion on his part. How he came to that conclusion I cannot confirm with any degree of certainty now, but as for all the information we had available and on the basis of everything that we were convinced of, I can say that that unit went out to training according to plan. Maybe General Dimitrijevic was not aware of that. These were young soldiers. No commander, no one would send a unit consisting of such soldiers for the sake of provocation. If somebody wanted to do something like that, then that would be done with a trained, well-equipped unit, but young soldiers, nobody would send them from training to provoke terrorists within the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But I think you will agree with me that the -- these events in Podujevo were causing what might be called a serious international or a serious incident and serious conflict with the KVM. Did you question General Dimitrijevic as to how he came to the conclusion that all of this was a pretense, the claim of a training exercise as a pretense?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that we had any kind of major clash with the mission because this activity had been something that the mission was notified of, including all the necessary information, and if we look at the talks with General Drewienkiewicz, the talks carried out between him and General Ojdanic, Chief of General Staff, he was not opposed to that at all, the unit going out there for training. He said that perhaps not the most convenient of moments had been selected, so that was the only disagreement and the only misunderstanding. General Ojdanic in his comments said that perhaps the marching route had not been successful one, it had not been the best choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you to have a look further down on that page or at page 16 of the B/C/S version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move to that and it's the second full paragraph, and this is page 14, the last two lines of page 14 and the first four lines of page 15 in the English which I'll read since it's difficult to put it on the -- on the screen at once.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said in response to General Dimitrijevic: "We have registered it and we have managed to avoid registering it as a combat group because it has been defined as though it was going into battle. Instead, we have registered it as some sort of mixed mechanised company that is on extended combat training in this training ground and how this will be will be decided down there. "That is all." Well, I take it you said that. Were you a participant in registering a combat group as a mixed or mechanised company on extended training?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's clearly defined here and on the basis of the report that this is a company that went out to train. According to the reports that we received, there were questions raised by the verifiers, was this a combat group or was this a unit according to establishment, because combat groups were temporary units, whereas the company that went out was an establishment unit defined as such and it went out with its full personnel according to establishment to train, not as a combat group to carry out some kind of combat activity. This unit was not capable of carrying out combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you said you registered it, does that mean you registered it with the KVM?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was defined and notification was sent to the OSCE mission saying that this was a company not a combat group and they had no objections because they checked the composition of that unit that was going out to fulfil that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did this group include elements of the 211th Armoured Brigade, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, this was a company, not a group, a company, from the 15th Armoured Brigade in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's move on to discuss the Grom plans. I think a point was made here earlier in the case that General Perisic in authorising the Grom plan therefore agreed that it was proper and not unconstitutional to engage the VJ in these activities, combat activities, in Kosovo without the calling of a state of emergency. So I think you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that in part of this question an institution is mentioned, or rather, the constitutional use of the army. So can Mr. Stamp say where he found his foundation for putting this kind of question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I believe when I think it is General DZ was cross-examined some time ago by counsel on behalf of Mr. Pavkovic that submission was made to him or that suggestion was made to him. I could find the precise reference later on, but I could take that out of the question and just proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The Grom 1 plan remained a plan, it was not implemented in 1998, was it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Grom or Thunder plan from 1998 had two stages. The first stage was called Thunder 1 and the other stage Thunder 2. That is how we defined it and that is how the directive defined it. It included security for the state border facing the Republic of Macedonia in the areas of responsibility of the 2nd and 3rd Army, then provided security for buildings and units in the area and that part of the plan was carried through. These were practically daily tasks. As for the second stage, Grom 2, it envisaged that if there were to be a radical deterioration of the situation and if there were to be radical activity on the part of terrorist forces on Kosovo to carry out a partial mobilisation in order to engage forces to deal with terrorism in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. When I said "Grom 1," I meant Grom 98. The first phase of Grom 98, did that -- was that implemented in the Pristina Corps area of operations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a few moments ago I said that these were the primary tasks in the area of securing the state border and that these tasks were carried through, that is to say that this activity was carried out. The Chief of General Staff defined in the directive that part of the tasks would be materialised in accordance with a special order of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we look at 4D137, please. If we could look at the first page of that document, both in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in the fourth paragraph it refers to: "The foreign factor deems the present activities by the Yugoslav Army in the territory of Kosovo to be justified and in the functions of the protection and sovereignty and integrity of the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The introduction of new Yugoslav Army units and their deployment in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija would be interpreted by NATO as an 'inappropriate use of force against innocent civilians.'" ? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you explain the meaning of that statement that: "The introduction of new Yugoslav Army units and their deployment and their deployment in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija would be interpreted by NATO as an'inappropriate use of force against innocent civilians'?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to this question is quite clearly given here. In the implementation of the task in Kosovo at that time, bringing up new units from the depth, from the 3rd Army or other units or other formations, would be interpreted by foreigners as inappropriate or excessive use of force against the terrorists. It is stated here in quotation marks "against innocent civilians" because the civilian population was used improperly as shields during various activities. This was analysed on a number of occasions because inhabited areas in all kinds of facilities where there were civilians were used. So that in fighting the terrorists there could be casualties among the civilian population that they put to this kind of use. So this could have been used as a pretext at the level of the international community to take some measures at the level of the Security Council or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: General, aren't you aware that starting on July 25 there was a major operation ongoing in Kosovo involving the use of the army in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were activities in fighting the Siptar [as interpreted] forces in Kosovo because terrorism was rampant at that time, and that is why plans were made - and you saw that for yourself, the directive Grom 98 - for the use of the army in accordance with this directive to suppress and eliminate terrorism as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The second phase of Grom 98 was not implemented in 1998; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You mean 1998? Because Grom 1998 was in 1998 and the second stage of Grom 98 -- well, mobilisation of units was not carried out, tasks were carried out by the peacetime units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have a look at P2166 a document which is minutes of a meeting of what is called the operations interdepartmental staff for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija on the 29th of October, 1999 [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You'll see present there among other persons is the Chief of Staff, General Perisic, the commander of the Pristina Corps at the time also General Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is presumably 1998?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I -- yes, the same page as in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, General Pavkovic spoke, and this is at page 2 of the B/C/S and at the end of page 1 going into page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So perhaps if we just look at page 2 of the English version, the top of page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "Speaking on behalf of the Joint Command for KiM, General Pavkovic reminded the members of the Operation Staff that the plan for suppressing terrorism in KiM had been carried out in five stages, an overall duration of 45 to 55 days. Implementation of the plan commenced on the 25th of July and the activities planned were completed on the 29th of October, 1998." Well, firstly, General, the operative plan in place in Kosovo that was being implemented in the fight against the KLA in July to October 1998 was not the Grom plan, but it is this plan that General Pavkovic speaks about. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I studied this document and I would like to ask you this -- what it says here that the supreme -- the Supreme Command or the supreme defence command should meet in June and that the decision was made at the briefing that measures should be taken to carry out counter-terrorist measures to suppress terrorism as soon as possible. And pursuant to this decision then in early June 1998, as you can see, every officer had the obligation in peacetime, too, pursuant to the Law on Army and Law on Defence and also the officers were bound by the rules of service of the Yugoslav Army, that measures should be taken in peacetime too to fight any sabotage terrorist or any other units. So commanding officers at all levels were bound by this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But you said earlier, yesterday I think it was, that the command of the 3rd Army, who at that time I think was General Pavkovic, was tasked to submit a plan in conformity with the Grom 98 plan on the 3rd of August, 1998. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. All I'm asking you is that having regard to what General Pavkovic says here, the plan that was being implemented on the ground --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think we have several inaccuracies here. First of all, the commander of the 3rd Army was not General Pavkovic at that time. I don't want the witness to be misled. He tried to actually say that, but Mr. Stamp interrupted him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that General Samardzic was the commander at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. The point I'm trying to make, though, General, which I just want to see if you accept and move on, that the plan that General Pavkovic is speaking of at this meeting which I just quoted was an operative plan for fighting the KLA in Kosovo in the summer and autumn of 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operative plan at the level of the General Staff for fighting terrorism in Kosovo was Grom 98 plan, and it was done in the second half of July. Activities were carried out in July, August, September, and later on. And if I may just make a comment, those initial activities carried out this thing that you're asking me about, this bound commanding officers at different levels to take measures to fight terrorism. With the orders, decisions on the basis of the assessment of the situation and then on the basis of that state that prevailed where terrorism was rampant, the General Staff issued a directive to carry out tasks in accordance with the Grom 98 directive. And the commander of the 3rd Army, General Samardzic, came to the General Staff, presented his decision about the use of forces, as I explained yesterday, focusing mostly on the Pristina Corps area of responsibility to destroy terrorist forces in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But General Pavkovic is speaking here of an operation that begun on the 25th of July, 1998, yet according to the Grom plan the command of the 3rd Army was supposed to submit his proposals by the 3rd of August. You will agree with me that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I think this is getting to the point of it being argumentative. The witness has now answered him three times that the plan being implemented was the Grom plan. He keeps going back to it thinking he can argue with the witness until he can get a different answer, but I think he's got his answer and needs to go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't think the witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How is it, Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, the particular question that's being asked at the moment contains more information that, on one view, is inconsistent with the previous answers. And therefore, we consider it appropriate to allow this question to be asked. So please continue, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: General, the question is that General Pavkovic in the -- in his speech in October 1998 referred to a plan which began on the 25th of July 1998 and continued for a period of 45-plus days as being the plan for the fight against the KLA or terrorism in Kosovo. How could it be that the Grom plan or the Grom 98 plan was a plan that was being implemented in the summer when the date when the commander of the 3rd Corps [as interpreted] was to submit his proposals in respect to the plan was as late as the 3rd of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no dilemma here. I was quite clear at the beginning of my reply. The Supreme Defence Council presented the situation as it was in Kosovo regarding the terrorism issue. The Chief of General Staff was notified about the situation and so was the commander of the 3rd Army. And since the focus of activities was in the area of responsibility of the Pristina Corps, the general made the decision to deal with this issue within his purview. Since this task was not fully carried out there was another assessment and -- from the General Staff and also other assessments, and on the basis of those assessments a decision was made to deal with this by issuing another order, and that was the directive 98 -- Grom 98, and the activities in Kosovo were carried out in accordance with this directive in stages. This is the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one correction in transcript. Page 111, line 21, should be 3rd Army --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think we all realise that, Mr. Visnjic. I have to confess, I'm now completely confused by the last answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: General, do you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, before I move on I note what Your Honour has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me ask the witness this. You say since that task was not fully carried out there was another assessment and from the General Staff and all other assessments, and on the basis of these assessments a decision was made to deal with this by issuing another order, and that was the directive 98. Now, are you dealing there with the question that was put to you by Mr. Stamp which was: The requirement for the commander of the 3rd Army was to submit his proposals by the 3rd of August? And here we have a situation where apparently the operation had begun on the 25th of July. How can that be so if we are -- if both relate to the same plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The activities carried out until that time, this was the obligation of the commander to deal with all those problems related to counter-terrorism in his area of responsibility and his purview in accordance with the rules of service and that's what he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That task --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- Just look back at the document where it said: "General Pavkovic reminded the members of the Operations Staff that the plan for suppressing terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija had been carried out in five stages with an overall duration of 45 to 55 days. Implementation of the plan commenced on 25 July and the activities planned were completed on the 29th of October." Now, how is that consistent with the idea that authority to go ahead with this had to be sought by the 3rd of August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think it's quite clear here what the essence is. Activities were carried out in the sphere of counter-terrorism not only in June but even earlier than that, and those activities were carried out over a wide area. The focus force was the Pristina Corps in accordance with the relevant decisions of the commander. When this task was carried out, then on the basis of the assessment by the General Staff that further measures should be taken and to regulate all that from the level of the General Staff on the basis of the overall situation that there should be a counter-terrorism operation in Kosovo in accordance with the directive that followed that was directive Grom 98. And I think that what other participants in the debate said, it is all in accordance with the Grom 98 directive at the time when the counter-terrorism operations were carried out in Kosovo and Metohija. So it was carried out according to the plan and directive issued by the General Staff from the beginning of August onwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that mean that on the 25th of July the Grom plan did not exist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Grom plan was approved on the 28th of July and the directive was signed on the 28th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, matters are getting, I think, wildly out of hand and I don't know quite how to deal with it. But it all, I believe, stems from the way Mr. Stamp approached this questioning. Clearly - and this was brought out in testimony in this case on the 23rd of January of 2007 - clearly Samardzic on the 29th of July ordered implementation of the Grom 1 plan --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Should this be said in the presence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think -- first of all, it shouldn't be done in the presence of the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He shouldn't be asking questions of the witness trying to trick him into an answer when he knows this document exists and is in the record and that's what's being -- that's what's unfair here and that's why it's getting out of hand. I'm willing to have the witness leave so I can complete my remarks if you want that to happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, which question do you think is misleading?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp has taken the position that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, tell me the question that you think is misleading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All the questions that have to do with whether or not Grom was implemented in 1998. There's a document that makes it very clear that it was issued by Samardzic and it's in evidence in the case and Mr. Stamp should know about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: To premise this entire questioning on the proposition that it wasn't implemented because the activity talked about on July 25th could not have been Grom and that's true, it could not have been because the order wasn't issued until the 29th. But every activity after that was Grom. I think that's fairly clear and I just think it's unfair the way Mr. Stamp is proceeding by ignoring the record, basically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stamp, you've completed your examination on this point, have you, or are you going to ask further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would like to ask a few more questions on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. And what do you have to say to Mr. Ackerman's objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I understand the objection. I can just say I wasn't attempting in any question to trick the witness; I was attempting to just get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't understand it either, but my colleagues would like to hear more about the point that's being made. I can't see a question, personally, that's inappropriate. I cannot see why when the date 25th July is related to the implementation of the plan, which could be for the suppressing of terrorism, why questions can't be asked about the relationship of the various dates, even allowing for the statement that is made in the Samardzic order. But is there anything else you want to say on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Anyone else want to comment on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't know if I've made myself clear. There was a plan to combat terrorism that preceded the Perisic directive that was the Grom plan. That directive went straight from Perisic to the 3rd Army --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, that's the very point that the questions were directed to, to establish that there was a plan other than the Grom plan. That's how this whole area of examination started.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, not true. It started with trying to establish that the Grom plan was never implemented; that's his point: Grom was never implemented. That's the thing he's trying to prove. It's not true. There's a document that proves that's not true. It was implemented and the witness told him that it was implemented in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: 4D140, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask you, Mr. Stamp, whether that's your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Phase 2 of the Grom plan was never implemented in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, the witness agreed with him that phase 2 was not implemented in 1998 his point was that phase 1 was not implemented in 1998, and you can go back and look at his question. That's what he asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's a question which the witness is capable of answering and he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, he did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, I won't have this batting back and forward across the courtroom. Please sit down until we read this document. Now, you can now assist us by the particular reference, please, to show that the plan was implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first thing you need to look at is first page which shows you that what Samardzic is talking about is the Grom plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Then if you will go to paragraph 5, Samardzic then sets out tasks for the Pristina Corps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I haven't got it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- Paragraph 5 yet on the screen. Which page is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's page 6 of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is ordering things to be done?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's right. He's setting out the tasks that the units need to carry out and implementation of the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where is the bit that tells that this was actually done?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This is an implementation -- an order like this is an implementation of the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Those were the questions: Was it implemented? Not what -- not: Did the units carry out the orders that were contained in it, although I'm convinced that they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We consider that the potential for confusion caused by the various dates before us justified Mr. Stamp in examining this issue closely. We do not think that there has been any attempt on his part to mislead the witness, and therefore we shall repel the objection. We will note the comments made, but we will have much more regard to the evidence that is ultimately placed before us. Mr. Stamp, do you want to complete this just now or do you want to deal with it tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think it's a convenient time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think it's a convenient time to pause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Obradovic, we need to conclude our sitting for today at this time. That means that you'll have to come back tomorrow to complete your evidence; that will be at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Meanwhile, overnight it is important that you should not have any discussion about the evidence with anyone at all. You can discuss anything else with whoever you like, but you must not with anyone discuss the evidence in this case. Now, would you please leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 6th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24
